name: Broad-facet nucleation kinetics
status: source-printed law with fitted or inverted temperature functions
proposition: Facet-normal growth follows Hertz-Knudsen kinetics with a facet-specific nucleation barrier before morphology is introduced.
governingRelation: v_n = alphaHK * vKin * sigmaSurface; alphaHK = A(T) * exp[-sigma0(T)/sigmaSurface]

variableStatus.v_n: measured locally in P8B facet series
variableStatus.A(T),sigma0(T): fits or inversions, not independent observations

assumptions: planar broad facet
source supersaturation can be mapped to local surface supersaturation
substrate and neighboring facets do not dominate the measured normal rate
predicts: exponential sensitivity to inverse surface supersaturation
different basal and prism curves at the same temperature
facet ordering can invert with temperature
cheapestDiscriminator: Without fitting either Phase 8 curve, forward-predict both planar-facet curves using one frozen source-to-surface mapping and report each residual series separately.
weakensOrRejects: systematic miss of both facet curves outside measurement and mapping uncertainty
a shared transport correction explains the apparent facet contrast without facet-specific kinetics
claimBoundary: development only; the same lineage supplied both the law and some fitted inputs

name: Width-conditioned structure-dependent attachment kinetics
phase9Role: newly separated candidate arm; proposed M-W
status: source-printed working hypothesis with unfrozen width scale; monograph-only input provisional pending newer-edition comparison
proposition: Narrowing a facet lowers its nucleation barrier and creates an edge-enhancing feedback that can sharpen plates, columns, and hollow rims.
governingRelation: sigma0(w)/sigma0Infinity = 1 - exp(-w/w0), coupled to alphaHK = A * exp[-sigma0(w)/sigmaSurface]

variableStatus.w: must be defined from physical facet geometry
variableStatus.w0: adjustable and not frozen by the source

assumptions: facet width is a sufficient structural state
one width law transfers across the tested geometry
edge premelting or surface diffusion is represented by the effective barrier change
predicts: thin facets grow faster at the same local supersaturation
positive sharpening feedback and possible history dependence
effect vanishes continuously for facets much wider than w0
cheapestDiscriminator: Compare spatial or rim-width trajectories at matched forcing; a single endpoint aspect ratio is not discriminating.
weakensOrRejects: no reproducible width dependence after conditioning on local supersaturation
one frozen w0 cannot predict both broad-facet rates and rim evolution
step-source location predicts the spatial growth profile without changing the barrier
claimBoundary: the Phase 6 no-dip ablation is an implementation contrast, not proof of physical SDAK; compare the newer monograph edition before freezing any monograph-only input

name: Step-source location and self-consistent facet flux
proposition: The position and strength of molecular step sources, coupled to the nonuniform diffusion field, determine whether a facet remains solid or hollows without requiring a width-dependent material law.
governingRelation: uniform flat-face advance requires alphaHK(x) * sigmaSurface(x) to be spatially uniform; a required alphaHK greater than one signals failure of the solid-face solution

variableStatus.rimWidth: directly observed in two native histories

assumptions: faceted continuum geometry
step supply can be represented separately from bulk diffusion
the measured rim corresponds to the modeled hollow-face boundary
predicts: different radial growth profiles for central versus edge step sources
hollowing onset when the solid-face solution becomes inadmissible
rim width is a state variable, not merely an endpoint shape label
cheapestDiscriminator: Acquire the full 2026 equation set, then use its companion histories only for source replay and rival-fit comparison around the 13,800 s intervention; require independent trigger evidence before causal promotion.
weakensOrRejects: predicted onset timing or rim direction is wrong under the recorded forcing
the required source-location change has no independent physical trigger
the same spatial profile is reproduced by fixed broad-facet kinetics after transport is resolved
claimBoundary: the companion archive alone does not define the 2026 integrator, kinetic closure, or hollowing rule; the same-lineage histories cannot independently confirm step-source causality

name: Mass-conditioned effective bulk transfer
status: empirical symbolic surrogate selected after neural-ODE training
proposition: Early small-crystal mass growth is better represented by a mass-conditioned effective transfer coefficient than by the continuum coefficient alone.

variableStatus.m: observed through a source-specific spherical initial-mass convention
variableStatus.coefficients: fit to neural-model outputs at training initial conditions

assumptions: individual particle is represented by one mass and capacitance
constant forcing per levitation history
transfer outside the paper's temperature or time domain is reported only as extrapolation
predicts: effective transfer increases with mass around a 3.108e-12 kg crossover
Phase 8 initial G/Gc spans about 0.378 to 1.312
same-condition runs 731A and 731B receive sharply different initial corrections solely from size
cheapestDiscriminator: After an experiment-ID overlap join, score 0-500 s on the six 205-240 K Phase 8 histories as the primary comparison. In each leave-one-history-out fold, estimate one global constant Gc rescale from the other five histories and evaluate it on the held-out history alongside continuum, Nelson-Baker and Lamb. Report hotter conditions and times after 500 s only as extrapolation; never pool points across histories.
weakensOrRejects: no per-history improvement over the leave-one-history-out constant rescale
residual supersaturation structure remains after conditioning on mass and Gc
measured trajectories lack the predicted increasing correction with size
performance disappears under initial-radius uncertainty
claimBoundary: bulk surrogate only; it has no facet, habit, initiation, support, or ventilation output and does not approach Gc at large mass; all Phase 8 comparisons remain development evidence

name: Coupled vapor and heat transport
status: established continuum transport with source-specific geometry factors
proposition: Observed size and aspect changes include separable resistance from vapor diffusion and latent-heat removal, so surface kinetics cannot be inferred from far-field forcing alone.
governingRelation: growth resistance is the sum of vapor-diffusion, thermal, and surface-kinetic terms under the selected geometry closure

variableStatus.vaporDiffusivity: calculated from temperature, pressure, and gas

assumptions: quasi-static fields
source geometry is represented or bounded
the one-factor Gonda-Komabayasi interventions preserve their reported fixed axis
predicts: lower vapor diffusivity or thermal conductivity lowers growth at fixed forcing
thermal and vapor interventions can change aspect differently through facet demand
transport-only corrections act on all mechanisms sharing the same field
cheapestDiscriminator: Reproduce the sign and relative scale of each one-factor intervention before fitting an interaction or changing surface kinetics.
weakensOrRejects: predicted sign is wrong for a controlled intervention
one common transport mapping cannot describe both fixed-conductivity and fixed-diffusivity families
apparent improvement requires changing a supposedly held-fixed source variable
claimBoundary: the Phase 8 source is not a crossed two-factor design and cannot identify an interaction term

name: Pressure-conditioned surface kinetics
phase9Role: source-model replay; M-PK remains source-limited until cross-pressure evidence is frozen
status: primary experiment plus model inversion; mechanism unresolved; Phase 8 selected trajectories are all at one bar
proposition: Changing background pressure alters prism attachment behavior beyond the change in vapor diffusivity alone.
governingRelation: alphaHKPrism(T,sigmaSurface,P) differs from a pressure-invariant alphaHKPrism while D varies approximately as 1/P
assumptions: cross-pressure apparatus effects are controlled
substrate support is represented consistently
surface supersaturation is solved rather than equated to far-field forcing
predicts: transport-only and pressure-conditioned trajectories separate at -5 C
the kinetic correction is facet-specific rather than a uniform growth rescale
cheapestDiscriminator: Replay the source-derived one-bar rule against both Phase 8 axes under one frozen geometry mapping; do not identify pressure dependence from that replay. Require a frozen cross-pressure trajectory not used to choose the rule before promoting M-PK as a pressure discriminator.
weakensOrRejects: D(P)-only matches both one-bar axes within uncertainty
the added rule improves one axis by degrading the other
the fitted correction fails a future pressure condition not used to choose it
claimBoundary: Phase 8 can replay or calibrate the source model but cannot identify pressure dependence because its selected trajectories contain no pressure intervention

name: Exact forcing-path fidelity
status: direct dynamic input test without a hidden memory state
proposition: A memoryless dynamic model receiving the measured forcing path predicts the observed trajectory better than the same model run under an endpoint-only forcing approximation.
governingRelation: state(t+dt) = F[state(t), T(t), forcing(t), geometry(t)] with no additional hidden memory variable

variableStatus.forcingPath: observed for Libbrecht series and categorical for the 48-to-20 archive

assumptions: forcing semantics and reference basis are known
events are synchronized to observations
numerical state transport is conservative under temperature changes
predicts: registered forcing events produce corresponding trajectory changes
constant-endpoint forcing misses some trajectory structure
cheapestDiscriminator: Compare the exact registered forcing path with an explicitly approximate endpoint-only replay. Treat improvement only as evidence for path fidelity, not memory.
weakensOrRejects: the exact path does not improve trajectory timing or direction
apparent event response vanishes after accounting for geometry and transport
claimBoundary: the archive labels 48 and 20 remain categorical until their supersaturation reference is established; this test cannot identify a hidden memory state

name: Internal memory beyond resolved path and geometry
phase9Role: second, conditional half of proposed M-H
status: project hypothesis requiring matched-endpoint or post-event relaxation evidence
proposition: After exact forcing, size, geometry and transport are represented, an additional observable state or relaxation process is needed to predict later growth.
governingRelation: state(t+dt) = F[resolvedState(t), forcing(t), memoryState(t)] with a named memory observable and relaxation timescale
assumptions: matched endpoints or post-event relaxation observations exist
resolved geometry and transport do not already encode the apparent lag
predicts: two matched resolved states retain different subsequent rates because their past paths differ
post-event residuals decay on a reproducible timescale
cheapestDiscriminator: Compare a Markov model using the exact path against one named stateful model on matched-endpoint or post-event relaxation rows. If the current records cannot establish a matched resolved state, mark memory non-identifiable rather than fitting it.
weakensOrRejects: the Markov exact-path model explains the post-event trajectory within uncertainty
the proposed state has no independent observable or stable relaxation timescale
apparent memory vanishes when geometry or transport is resolved
claimBoundary: path-fidelity improvement is not evidence for memory; any same-lineage fit remains model development

name: Ventilation-conditioned transport
status: controlled qualitative evidence; full quantitative source unavailable locally
proposition: Relative air motion changes boundary-layer transport enough to alter growth rate and sometimes habit, making still-air and free-fall targets non-interchangeable.
governingRelation: effective vapor and heat transfer factors depend on Reynolds and Schmidt or Prandtl numbers and crystal geometry

variableStatus.airSpeed: controlled in Keller-Hallett but absent from most Phase 8 records

assumptions: relative velocity and orientation are known
flow remains in the closure's Reynolds-number range
riming and turbulence are excluded
predicts: increased air speed raises transport and can shift skeletal transition boundaries
free-fall growth cannot be scored as a still-air specimen without a low-Re bound
cheapestDiscriminator: Acquire the full controlled-velocity paper or derive a conservative low-Re ineligibility bound; do not fit a quantitative ventilation arm from the abstract.
weakensOrRejects: a documented bound makes ventilation negligible over a declared subset
predicted velocity response has the wrong sign or scale in a controlled series
claimBoundary: qualitative gate only with current source access

name: Initiation state beyond size and exposure
status: direct aggregate contrast with major confounding
proposition: Droplet freezing or seed activation creates a persistent initial structural state that affects later habit beyond initial size and accumulated mass exposure.
governingRelation: growth law includes a named initiation-state variable after matching size, forcing, and exposure
assumptions: reported classes correspond to a persistent physical difference
protocol differences can be reproduced or bounded
aggregate ranges are not treated as individual rows
predicts: matched size and exposure still leave an initiation-conditioned habit contrast
the named state intervention changes more than a generic noise seed
cheapestDiscriminator: First reproduce the two size/exposure protocols with no initiation-state term; add one named state only if the aggregate direction remains unexplained.
weakensOrRejects: size and exposure reproduce the reported direction
the new state cannot be tied to an observable or intervention
the result depends on inventing unreported group denominators
claimBoundary: reported ranges support a directional development test, not a distribution fit or causal effect size

name: Low-cost latent-heating correction
phase9Role: direction-only prior until an exact-condition resistance calculation is frozen; proposed M-LH
proposition: Latent heat raises the crystal surface temperature and reduces diffusion-limited growth by a calculable resistance factor.
governingRelation: diffusion-limited multiplier approximately 1/(1+chi0), with source anchors chi0 about 0.8 at -1 C and 0.4 at -10 C
assumptions: quasi-static thermal field
small enough temperature rise for the linearized closure
geometry factor transfers to the tested specimen
predicts: ignoring heating overpredicts growth
effect strengthens toward warmer temperatures and lower thermal conductivity
cheapestDiscriminator: Use the two printed anchors only as a direction and rough-scale check. Before quantitative comparison at -7 C or -15 C, calculate the multiplier from the printed vapor-plus-thermal resistance equation with the exact source geometry and conductivity; do not interpolate the two anchors.
weakensOrRejects: wrong intervention sign
the exact-condition resistance calculation falls outside the source anchor behavior without explanation
improvement comes only from retuning facet kinetics
claimBoundary: anchors are approximate and do not define an interpolated universal curve or an executable target-condition multiplier

name: Curvature equilibrium correction
status: established interfacial thermodynamics without matched Phase 8 validation target
proposition: High positive curvature raises local equilibrium vapor pressure and suppresses growth at small tips.
governingRelation: sigmaEffective = sigmaSurface - d_sv*kappa; kappa = 2/R for a sphere
assumptions: continuum curvature is meaningful at the grid scale
surface energy is isotropic or its anisotropy is specified
curvature estimator is numerically stable
predicts: suppression scales inversely with radius
effect is small for 5.8-12 um equivalent spheres but potentially material near submicron tips
cheapestDiscriminator: Use manufactured curved interfaces and grid-convergence tests; do not claim source validation from Phase 8.
weakensOrRejects: term fails its analytic spherical limit
apparent benefit disappears with grid refinement
no matched measurement is acquired for physical promotion
claimBoundary: can improve numerical physics without earning a Phase 8 measurement agreement

name: Printed two-branch prism kinetics
proposition: A two-branch prism barrier captures a temperature-dependent kinetic regime not represented by the broad branch alone.
governingRelation: source-printed piecewise or two-branch sigma0Prism(T) prescription
assumptions: source temperature and supersaturation mappings are preserved
branch selection is not tuned after campaign scoring
predicts: localized residual improvement in its stated temperature domain
no improvement outside the branch domain
cheapestDiscriminator: After the broad-facet baseline, freeze the printed formula and compare per-series residuals without refitting.
weakensOrRejects: no improvement on any direct prism-rate series
improvement requires changing source coefficients
gain is confined to the same rows that supplied the fit
claimBoundary: not independent evidence; M2-like parameter families are not a no-SDAK control

name: Face-dependent quasi-liquid-layer mechanism
phase9Role: qualitative mechanism prior, not an implementation arm or quantitative discriminator
proposition: Different molecular ordering and quasi-liquid-layer behavior on basal and prism faces can generate face-dependent attachment kinetics and temperature transitions.
governingRelation: molecular free-energy, ordering, and incorporation statistics inform an effective alphaHK(T,face), but no project-scale closure is yet frozen
assumptions: force field and simulated scale capture the relevant interface physics
a defensible coarse-graining maps molecular observables to continuum kinetics
predicts: face-dependent transition temperatures and incorporation behavior
a molecular rationale for effective facet laws
strongestRivals: effective nucleation law without a unique molecular interpretation
cheapestDiscriminator: Use the reported face/temperature ordering only as a qualitative consistency screen; do not score macroscopic vapor-growth rates until a defensible scale bridge is frozen.
weakensOrRejects: wrong qualitative face or temperature ordering
no quantitative bridge to alphaHK or sigma0
prediction depends strongly on an unvalidated potential
claimBoundary: knowledge support only; simulation agreement is not a measured macroscopic kinetics calibration

name: Phenomenological mesoscopic control
phase9Role: permanent differential control, not physical mechanism
proposition: A compact diffusion-plus-threshold rule can reproduce qualitative morphology classes without claiming that its threshold parameters are physical attachment kinetics.
governingRelation: published Gravner-Griffeath masked diffusion, freezing, attachment-threshold, and melting cycle
assumptions: qualitative morphology is the requested comparison
no physical units or validation label are inferred
predicts: rich morphology under parameter changes
useful differential behavior when physical surface exchange acts strangely
strongestRivals: any physical mechanism arm for quantitative measurement comparison
cheapestDiscriminator: Retain as a visual and implementation control; mark it protocol-ineligible for physical-time, facet-rate, or mass-history scores.
weakensOrRejects: none as a physical theory because it is not promoted as one
any attempt to map its thresholds to alphaHK without a source-derived bridge
claimBoundary: shape resemblance is not physical validation and cannot serve as a no-SDAK control
